html:
SMTO-AUT-0035 — SMTO couldn't get an answer from Google sign-in

GUID: 578abcf4-2f62-5e70-a043-0c3e37f12867
Slug: google-provider-unavailable
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: google-workspace

What happened

  • SMTO contacted Google to finish or renew your Google sign-in, but the connection failed or Google's reply couldn't be used. Your saved Google connection wasn't changed, and the Google request you asked for wasn't made.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the computer running SMTO is online and can open Google websites, for example accounts.google.com in a web browser on that computer. SMTO's server talks to Google directly to confirm or renew your sign-in.
  2. If your network needs a proxy or blocks Google sign-in pages, tell the person who manages SMTO. SMTO doesn't use proxy settings for this connection, so a blocked or filtered network makes it fail every time.
  3. If you were connecting an account, ask SMTO to connect it again and finish the new Google sign-in link within ten minutes. The earlier sign-in link was used up when this failed and can't be reused.
  4. If a Task was using Gmail, Google Calendar or Google Drive, check whether its earlier steps already made changes, then ask again in a new message. SMTO stopped before this step reached Google, but steps before it may have finished.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows the Google account as connected, or the Google request finishes with results.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the time it failed, to the person who manages SMTO. Never paste Google passwords, sign-in codes or tokens into a conversation to get around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Google token endpoint exchange (authorization-code completion or refresh-token renewal) failed before a usable token bundle was returned, for example an unreachable network, the 30-second deadline, an unexpected HTTP status, an oversized body or an unreadable response.

What this means

  • The Google adapter caught an authorization exchange failure before receiving a usable token bundle; the wrapper does not identify a specific network cause. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • The Google adapter caught an authorization exchange failure before receiving a usable token bundle; the wrapper does not identify a specific network cause.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the exchange phase, trusted endpoint availability and public provider status; do not assume the account password is wrong.

How to fix it

  • Verify outbound HTTPS from the Server process to oauth2.googleapis.com; the auth Transport sets trust_env=False, so HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY variables are ignored. Rule out Google-side 5xx or 429 responses, then restart consent with auth.google_connect (the pending state was already consumed) or rerun the read; no tokens were saved.
  • Check network access to Google OAuth endpoints and retry when available.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm account identity and required features before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended Google token exchange returns a validated response through the configured transport.

What not to do

  • Do not expose client secrets, tokens, codes or PKCE verifiers.
  • Do not switch accounts or repeat uncertain mutations automatically.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
